question.prompt: Which tasks should `todo list --overdue` include? This determines the filter’s core observable behavior.

options.label: Incomplete, before today
options.description: Include only unfinished tasks whose due date is strictly earlier than today; due-today, completed, and undated tasks are excluded.

options.label: All before today
options.description: Include completed and unfinished tasks whose due date is strictly earlier than today; due-today and undated tasks are excluded.

options.label: Incomplete, due by today
options.description: Include only unfinished tasks whose due date is today or earlier; completed and undated tasks are excluded.

question.prompt: How should `--overdue` interact with the existing `--priority` and `--due` filters?

options.label: Combine with both
options.description: Apply all supplied filters conjunctively; `--due DATE --overdue` matches only when that exact date is before today and the task is incomplete.

options.label: Priority only
options.description: Allow `--overdue` with `--priority`, but reject its use with `--due` as a usage error.

options.label: Use alone
options.description: Reject `--overdue` whenever either existing filter is also supplied.

question.prompt: How should users activate the overdue filter? This determines parsing, help text, and invalid-input behavior.

options.label: Boolean flag
options.description: Use `todo list --overdue` as a value-free `store_true` flag; this matches the request’s wording and conventional filter syntax.

contract.summary: Add a value-free `--overdue` boolean filter to `todo list` while preserving existing behavior. An overdue task is incomplete, has a due date strictly before the current UTC calendar date, and may be filtered conjunctively with `--priority` and `--due`. Production code must use UTC through an internal injectable or patchable date provider so tests are deterministic. The persisted task schema, row format, established sorting, exit behavior, and standard-library-only constraint remain unchanged.
confirmed_decisions: `--overdue` is a value-free boolean flag on the `list` command.
A task is overdue only when it is incomplete and its due date is strictly earlier than today.
Tasks due today are not overdue.
Completed tasks, including completed tasks with past due dates, are not overdue.
`--overdue`, `--priority`, and `--due` combine conjunctively when supplied together.
`--overdue --due DATE` matches only incomplete tasks whose due date exactly equals DATE and DATE is strictly before today.
Today is the current UTC calendar date.
Production date lookup uses an internal injectable or patchable seam for deterministic tests.
Filtering remains read-only and does not add an `overdue` field to persisted task data.
Existing row formatting, post-filter sort order, empty-result behavior, storage behavior, and exit-code conventions must remain unchanged.
No runtime dependency may be added; Python 3.10 or newer remains supported.
Implementation is authorized by the original request.
acceptance_checks: With the injected UTC date set to 2026-07-19 and tasks consisting of incomplete due 2026-07-18, incomplete due 2026-07-19, incomplete due 2026-07-20, incomplete undated, completed due 2026-07-18, and completed undated, running `todo list --overdue` prints only the incomplete task due 2026-07-18, using the unchanged tab-separated row format, and returns 0.
With the injected UTC date set to 2026-07-19 and incomplete overdue tasks of multiple priorities, `todo list --overdue --priority high` prints only high-priority overdue tasks and returns 0.

With the injected UTC date set to 2026-07-19, `todo list --overdue --due 2026-07-18` prints only incomplete tasks due exactly 2026-07-18, while `todo list --overdue --due 2026-07-19` prints nothing; both commands return 0.

With the injected UTC date set to 2026-07-19, `todo list --overdue --priority high --due 2026-07-18` applies all three filters conjunctively and prints only incomplete high-priority tasks due exactly 2026-07-18.

When multiple tasks match `--overdue`, output retains the established ordering: incomplete state, descending priority, ascending due date with undated tasks last, then ascending ID; because overdue excludes done and undated tasks, the remaining effective ordering is priority, due date, then ID.
Running `todo list --overdue` when the store does not exist prints nothing to stdout or stderr, returns 0, and does not create the store file.
Running `todo list --overdue` when no tasks qualify prints nothing and returns 0 without modifying the store.
Running `todo list --overdue true` is rejected by argument parsing as unexpected input and returns usage exit code 2 without propagating `SystemExit` or modifying the store.
Existing valid and invalid `--due` behavior remains unchanged, including exact calendar-date validation and usage exit code 2 for invalid dates.
A before-and-after byte comparison of the store around every `list` command using `--overdue`, alone or combined with other filters, shows no persisted changes.
Existing list commands without `--overdue` preserve their filtering, output, sorting, and exit behavior, and the full existing test suite plus new overdue regression tests passes.

The README documents `todo list [--priority {low,medium,high}] [--due YYYY-MM-DD] [--overdue]`, the strict-before-current-UTC-date rule, exclusion of completed and undated tasks, and conjunctive combination with existing filters.
